```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(mysterynpi)
```

`R/agreement.R` has carried this sentence since the rule was removed from the
real pipeline:

> **No edit-distance tolerance.** A one-edit rule was added and removed the
> same day: measured, it changed 64 of 30,740 candidate pairs and was worth 22
> records, while admitting pairs that are genuinely different given names
> (`JULIA`/`JULIE`, `LEE`/`LEA`, `ANN`/`ANNE`).

That is a performance claim about an alternative implementation, and until now
it was prose. This vignette is the measurement, on the 190 pairs of
`ROSTER_BENCHMARK` whose truth is known by construction.

## Why this is a vignette and not a function

`tests/testthat/test-no-fuzzy.R` refuses any approximate-matching call
anywhere in `R/`: source scan, parse-tree scan, and call-graph reachability
over the installed namespace, with no exempt module. An exported
`compare_with_edit_distance()` was written first and the guard rejected it,
correctly — a package whose argument is that approximate spelling similarity
has no place in identity resolution should not ship fuzzy machinery reachable
from its own namespace, not even to argue against it.

A vignette is code you can run and read, and it is outside the namespace. The
comparison lives here; the rule stays absolute there.

## The two approaches

The package's decision is `benchmark_decisions()`: any conflicting axis
rejects (a middle-name conflict excused when the roster's middle token *is*
the registry surname), a pair without both surname and given corroboration
goes to review, a gender conflict goes to review rather than deletion.

The baseline is the simplest credible alternative and needs no new dependency:
accept when the two full names are within one edit of each other.

```{r}
b <- ROSTER_BENCHMARK
rules_accept <- benchmark_decisions(b) == "accept"

roster_full <- normalize_string(b$roster_name)
reference_full <- normalize_string(paste(b$npi_first, b$npi_last))
edits <- vapply(seq_along(roster_full), function(i)
  as.integer(utils::adist(roster_full[i], reference_full[i])[1, 1]), integer(1))
edit_accept <- !is.na(edits) & edits <= 1L
```

```{r}
score <- function(accept, truth) {
  tp <- sum(accept & truth == "match")
  fp <- sum(accept & truth == "nonmatch")
  fn <- sum(!accept & truth == "match")
  data.frame(accepted = sum(accept),
             precision = round(tp / max(tp + fp, 1L), 3),
             recall = round(tp / max(tp + fn, 1L), 3),
             false_accepts = fp)
}
rbind(`mysterynpi rules` = score(rules_accept, b$truth),
      `edit distance <= 1` = score(edit_accept, b$truth))
```

The baseline accepts a third as many true matches and makes false accepts the
rules do not make.

## Where the false accepts land

```{r}
false_accepts <- b[edit_accept & b$truth == "nonmatch",
                   c("family", "roster_name", "npi_first", "npi_last")]
false_accepts$edits <- edits[edit_accept & b$truth == "nonmatch"]
false_accepts
```

They concentrate in the `spelling-trap` family, which is the `JULIA`/`JULIE`
case the comment describes: one edit apart, and different people.

## Where each approach loses the other's matches

```{r}
differs <- rules_accept != edit_accept
data.frame(family = b$family[differs], truth = b$truth[differs],
           rules = ifelse(rules_accept[differs], "accept", "-"),
           edit = ifelse(edit_accept[differs], "accept", "-"))[1:12, ]
```

Edit distance misses what structure explains: a maiden surname in a middle
slot, a nickname, concatenated initials, a credential suffix, a formatting
difference. None of those are spelling errors, and a distance threshold loose
enough to catch them is loose enough to accept `JULIA`/`JULIE`.

## What this does not show

The corpus is built from this package's own defect taxonomy, so clean
separation is **consistency, not proof of generality** — the same caveat
`vignette("roster-benchmark")` states. It also compares against *one*
alternative. It is not a comparison with
[reclin2](https://cran.r-project.org/package=reclin2) or
[fastLink](https://cran.r-project.org/package=fastLink), which solve the
scoring problem this package deliberately stops short of; `DESCRIPTION` draws
that boundary and this vignette does not cross it.
